svg.title: From deterministic to non-deterministic logic in Power Platform
svg.desc: A horizontal spectrum in three zones. Left, deterministic: the same input always gives the same output, and the logic can be read, tested exhaustively and audited. Power Platform examples: business rules, Power Fx formulas, plug-ins and custom APIs, cloud flows and agent flows without AI actions, alternate keys and duplicate rules, SLA calculations, classic orchestration where topics fire on trigger phrases. Middle, hybrid: a deterministic process with an AI step whose output is constrained and checked. Examples: a prompt with JSON output inside a flow with a guard, Power Fx AI functions such as AIClassify with a fixed category list, generative answers inside a topic, prompts as workflow nodes. Right, non-deterministic: the model chooses what to do and what to say. Examples: generative orchestration choosing topics, tools, knowledge and agents by their descriptions; agents on the GitHub Copilot harness that plan multi-step work; free-text drafts and summaries. Below, rows compare the zones. Repeatability: exact, exact around the AI step, varies. Testing: unit tests of rules, tests plus an evaluation set, evaluation sets and monitoring. Explaining a result: read the rule, read the rule plus the model answer kept as data, reconstruct from logs. Handles ambiguity and free text: poorly, at the AI step, well. Cost and latency per call: very low, plus one model call, several model calls. Arrows say: move logic left when a rule exists, the outcome is consequential or must be audited; move right only for what rules cannot express, and keep a deterministic boundary around it.
svg.text: Where does the logic run? Deterministic, hybrid, non-deterministic
Cedar: DR rules, routing, status mapping
deterministic process, one AI step, checked
the model chooses what to do and say
Move logic LEFT when a rule exists, when the outcome is consequential (money, safety, a customer, a partner, the system of record),
or when it must be explained and audited. Move RIGHT only for what rules cannot express (free text, language, judgement on
unstructured input), and keep a deterministic boundary around it: closed outputs, a guard, a human step, an evaluation gate.
